steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ergonomics ensures products fit the human body — anthropometric data (body measurements) informs design decisions.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The design process for products: brief, research, ideation, development, prototyping, testing, refinement, manufacture.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Prototyping tests ideas before commitment to production — models can be rough (card) or refined (3D printed).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Sustainable design considers the full lifecycle: material sourcing, manufacture, use, and end-of-life disposal or recycling.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring product design and development. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with product design and development. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with product design and development. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to product design and development, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined o | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
